stem:
Sienna, 15, has eaten almost nothing for 6 days. She says she feels fine and wants to go home.

| Measurement | Value | Reference range |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Weight loss over 4 months | 12 kg | — |
| Current weight | 43 kg | — |
| Heart rate, lying | 44/min | — |
| Heart rate, standing | 80/min | — |
| Blood pressure | 86/52 mmHg | — |
| Temperature | 35.3 °C | — |
| Potassium | 3.3 mmol/L | 3.5-5.0 |
| Phosphate | 0.82 mmol/L | 0.9-1.6 |
| Glucose | 3.9 mmol/L | — |

Which management plan is most appropriate?

options.label: A
options.text: Weekly family-based treatment, with GP checks in between
options.explanation: Family-based treatment is first line for a medically stable adolescent. A heart rate under 50, temperature under 35.5°C, low phosphate and rapid weight loss mark instability, which needs admission.

options.label: B
options.text: Admit, replace electrolytes, give thiamine and start NG feeds
options.explanation: She is medically unstable and at high refeeding risk. Start replacement of phosphate and potassium, give thiamine before feeding, and commence a supervised NG feeding plan with cardiac and electrolyte monitoring.

options.label: C
options.text: Admit and hold feeds until her electrolytes are normal
options.explanation: Withholding nutrition prolongs starvation and keeps her unstable. Deficits are corrected and phosphate and thiamine given before the first feed, which then starts without waiting for normal results.

options.label: D
options.text: Admit and start meals at 600 kcal a day, raised weekly
options.explanation: Prolonged severe calorie restriction leaves her underfed. NSW guidance uses continuous NG feeding prescribed for age and refeeding risk, with electrolyte replacement and close monitoring.

options.label: E
options.text: Admit and give a 20 mL/kg saline bolus for her bradycardia
options.explanation: Her bradycardia is an adaptation to starvation, not a sign of shock, so a bolus is not indicated. A starved heart tolerates a fluid load poorly.

context: Medical instability in anorexia nervosa requires admission, correction of electrolyte deficits, thiamine and supervised nutritional rehabilitation with close monitoring.
